title: Graduated rollout SDK primitives with shadowing, telemetry-driven guards, and auto-rollback
creator: Alec Moreno
description: Deliver an ergonomic set of API and SDK primitives that let teams run graduated rollouts (canary -> ramp -> full), A/B tests and shadow traffic experiments with built-in telemetry guards and automatic rollback. This ticket specifies the product contract, high-level API shapes, permission model, suggested client helpers and the safety thresholds that should be implemented by the runtime. The goal is to enable safe, repeatable rollouts with minimal operator overhead and clear audit trails.
acceptance_criteria: API endpoints exist for creating/updating/observing rollouts and traffic policies (/rollouts, /rollouts/:id/traffic, /rollouts/:id/monitoring)
SDK exposes high-level helpers for common patterns: startCanary, promoteStep, abortRollout, shadowTraffic, startABTest
Idempotency semantics documented and implemented: client-provided idempotency token + server dedupe window, concurrent updates guarded by version/etag
Permission model defined: rollout.read, rollout.write, rollout.execute, rollout.audit and enforced by Private/Dedicated control plane
Telemetry and guard conditions defined and connected to auto-rollback actions (pause, rollback to previous version, alert) with configurable thresholds
End-to-end integration demonstrated with example app and automated integration test that simulates a degrading canary and triggers rollback
notes: PM proposal v1 posted in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ML/Graduated+Rollouts+API (internal) — contains example flow diagrams and UX wireframes.
Design flagged that rollout timeline UI needs explicit preview of what will happen at each step (screenshot + tooltip). See design ticket DES-412 for mocks.
Engineering requested a minimal MVP surface: create/read/list rollouts + apply traffic changes + observe metrics. Advanced automation (auto-promote) deferred to follow-up.
We will surface evaluation-set results and synthetic quality checks as first-class signals for rollback; skilled teams can attach custom evaluator webhooks.
Proposed idempotency: header X-Rollout-Idempotency-Key. Server keeps dedupe keys for 24 hours by default, configurable per-tenant.
Optimistic concurrency: rollout resource includes integer 'version' and updates must provide expected_version. Conflicts return 409 and include latest resource snapshot link.
Telemetry metrics to emit from runtime: rollout.traffic_split, rollout.eval.score, rollout.error_rate, rollout.latency.p95, rollout.rollback.trigger. These map to Console dashboards and alert rules.

Suggested default rollback triggers: (1) absolute error rate > 1% AND >= 2x baseline sustained for 5 minutes; OR (2) p95 latency increase >= 30% over baseline for 5 minutes; OR (3) evaluation-set quality delta worse than configured threshold (per-eval) in two consecutive measurement windows.
Auto-rollback actions: create rollback audit entry, switch traffic back to previous model variant, mark rollout as 'rolled_back', notify on-call + owners, and create incident link if severity high.

For shadow experiments: runtime should support mirrored copies of requests (headers redacted per policy) and limit mirror sampling rate. Shadow runs are non-blocking and do not affect latency for real traffic.

Idempotent SDK helpers should surface deterministic operation IDs for client retries and exponential backoff for network errors; they should also offer a 'dryRun' option for previewing changes without applying them.
Security review required: true. KMS/HSM considerations for audit logs and PII redaction in shadowed payloads must be documented.
Dependencies: ENG-11890 (rollout backend primitives), ENG-12120 (telemetry pipeline), ENG-12277 (authz scopes).
Example GH PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/467 (prototype of rollout API schema)
implementation_notes: API shape: POST /rollouts creates a rollout spec with ordered steps: [{type: 'canary', pct: 5, duration_minutes: 30, eval_set_id: 'ev-12'}, ...].
Traffic API: PATCH /rollouts/:id/traffic accepts delta objects and optional idempotency_key header. Server returns operation id for polling.

SDK helper signatures (suggested): startCanary(model, variant, pct, durationMinutes, evalSetId, opts), promoteStep(rolloutId, stepIndex, opts), pauseRollout(rolloutId, reason), abortRollout(rolloutId, reason).
Permissions: runtime must check 'rollout.execute' for actions that change traffic and 'rollout.write' for spec updates; audit logs must record actor, ip, and idempotency key.
Backwards compatibility: older client SDKs calling traffic endpoints without idempotency must still succeed; server logs should mark non-idempotent operations for migration telemetry.
Audit trail: every traffic mutation stored as immutable event (actor, timestamp, before, after, operation_id). Provide an endpoint to stream events for compliance exports.
Testing plan: unit tests for idempotency behavior, integration test that simulates stepwise increase with one noisy canary triggering rollback, e2e with example app using SDK helpers.
Observability: add rollout-specific tags to metrics and traces (rollout_id, step_index, model_variant). Implement sampling rules for trace volume when shadowing high qps.
Fallback behavior: if runtime cannot determine previous stable model, rollback should pause and mark for manual intervention and escalate via alerting policy.
Rate limits: enforce per-tenant mutation rate for rollouts to avoid accidental rapid flapping via automation (default 10 mutations/minute).
